symbols.name: wire count
symbols.meaning: The number of wires of the network under consideration, W_b for the bit network or W_c for the complex one (not a stream count).
symbols.quote: The labelling chooses the frames of [Frames on wire arrays](array-frames.md) so that a network of $W\in\{W_{\rm b},W_{\rm c}\}$ wires costs $s<Wm$ smaller calls, the saving the recursion needs.

symbols.name: smaller-call count
symbols.meaning: The total number of smaller calls made by the edges of the network under consideration.
symbols.quote: The labelling chooses the frames of [Frames on wire arrays](array-frames.md) so that a network of $W\in\{W_{\rm b},W_{\rm c}\}$ wires costs $s<Wm$ smaller calls, the saving the recursion needs.

symbols.name: subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of a space with a symmetric bilinear form; later a label.
symbols.quote: A subspace $U$ is *nondegenerate* when the form restricted to it is; then the space is the orthogonal sum $U\perp U^\perp$.

symbols.name: first vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of F, the first argument of the bit form (not the polynomial variable).
symbols.quote: Bit labels use $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $x\cdot y-\frac19(x\cdot\mathbf 1)(y\cdot\mathbf 1)$ for vectors $x,y\in F$, nondegenerate as its matrix fixes vectors orthogonal to $\mathbf 1=(1,\dots,1)$ and scales $\mathbf 1$ by $1-h/9=-91/9$.

symbols.name: second vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of F, the second argument of the bit form (not the ring variable).
symbols.quote: Bit labels use $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $x\cdot y-\frac19(x\cdot\mathbf 1)(y\cdot\mathbf 1)$ for vectors $x,y\in F$, nondegenerate as its matrix fixes vectors orthogonal to $\mathbf 1=(1,\dots,1)$ and scales $\mathbf 1$ by $1-h/9=-91/9$.

symbols.name: all-ones vector
symbols.meaning: The vector of F whose entries are all 1.
symbols.quote: Bit labels use $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $x\cdot y-\frac19(x\cdot\mathbf 1)(y\cdot\mathbf 1)$ for vectors $x,y\in F$, nondegenerate as its matrix fixes vectors orthogonal to $\mathbf 1=(1,\dots,1)$ and scales $\mathbf 1$ by $1-h/9=-91/9$.

symbols.name: triple
symbols.meaning: A three-element subset of [h], an element of the triple set (not a convolution length).
symbols.quote: Triples $S,S'\in\mathcal T$ have indicator vectors $t_S,t_{S'}$ with dot product $|S\cap S'|$ and entry sums $3$, so $\langle t_S,t_{S'}\rangle=|S\cap S'|-1$, or $|S\cap S'|\bmod2$ over $\mathbb F_2$.

symbols.name: second triple
symbols.meaning: Another three-element subset of [h].
symbols.quote: Triples $S,S'\in\mathcal T$ have indicator vectors $t_S,t_{S'}$ with dot product $|S\cap S'|$ and entry sums $3$, so $\langle t_S,t_{S'}\rangle=|S\cap S'|-1$, or $|S\cap S'|\bmod2$ over $\mathbb F_2$.

symbols.name: indicator vector
symbols.meaning: The indicator vector in F of the triple S.
symbols.quote: Triples $S,S'\in\mathcal T$ have indicator vectors $t_S,t_{S'}$ with dot product $|S\cap S'|$ and entry sums $3$, so $\langle t_S,t_{S'}\rangle=|S\cap S'|-1$, or $|S\cap S'|\bmod2$ over $\mathbb F_2$.

symbols.name: first factor subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of a tensor power of F; in the bracket notation, a subspace of F.
symbols.quote: Dimension counting rests on three facts about [tensor products of subspaces](tensor-product-of-spaces.md): for subspaces $E,E',G$ of tensor powers of $F$, $\dim(E\otimes G)=\dim E\cdot\dim G$; the form multiplies factorwise, so products of nondegenerate subspaces are nondegenerate; and $(E\perp E')\otimes G=(E\otimes G)\perp(E'\otimes G)$.

symbols.name: second factor subspace
symbols.meaning: Another subspace of a tensor power of F; in the bracket notation, a subspace of F containing E.
symbols.quote: Dimension counting rests on three facts about [tensor products of subspaces](tensor-product-of-spaces.md): for subspaces $E,E',G$ of tensor powers of $F$, $\dim(E\otimes G)=\dim E\cdot\dim G$; the form multiplies factorwise, so products of nondegenerate subspaces are nondegenerate; and $(E\perp E')\otimes G=(E\otimes G)\perp(E'\otimes G)$.

symbols.name: other factor subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of a tensor power of F; in the bracket notation, a subspace of F.
symbols.quote: Dimension counting rests on three facts about [tensor products of subspaces](tensor-product-of-spaces.md): for subspaces $E,E',G$ of tensor powers of $F$, $\dim(E\otimes G)=\dim E\cdot\dim G$; the form multiplies factorwise, so products of nondegenerate subspaces are nondegenerate; and $(E\perp E')\otimes G=(E\otimes G)\perp(E'\otimes G)$.

symbols.name: label space
symbols.meaning: The label space F tensor F tensor F, of dimension m.
symbols.quote: Labels lie in $\mathcal F=F\otimes F\otimes F$, of dimension $h^3=m$.

symbols.name: data line
symbols.meaning: The line spanned by the tensor product of the indicators of the three triples of the data index a.
symbols.quote: With $U_a=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$, the terminal labels are

symbols.name: total loss
symbols.meaning: The total dimension lost on the decreasing edges of the network under consideration.
symbols.quote: If decreasing edges lose $L\in\{L_{\rm b},L_{\rm c}\}$ dimensions in total, absolute changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$.

symbols.name: bit loss
symbols.meaning: The total dimension lost on the decreasing edges of the bit network.
symbols.quote: If decreasing edges lose $L\in\{L_{\rm b},L_{\rm c}\}$ dimensions in total, absolute changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$.

symbols.name: complex loss
symbols.meaning: The total dimension lost on the decreasing edges of the complex network.
symbols.quote: If decreasing edges lose $L\in\{L_{\rm b},L_{\rm c}\}$ dimensions in total, absolute changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$.

symbols.name: bit smaller-call count
symbols.meaning: The number of smaller calls made by the edges of the bit network.
symbols.quote: Bit-network edges cost their absolute change plus one call per input $X_a$ (below), so $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-(N-2L_{\rm b})$: to save, the labels must confine all loss to one small edge.

symbols.name: complex smaller-call count
symbols.meaning: The number of smaller calls made by the edges of the complex network.
symbols.quote: [Binary phase frames](phase-frames.md) give the complex network, without the source extra, $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$.

symbols.name: stage index
symbols.meaning: The index 1, 2 or 3 of the stage, which varies the coordinate a_j.
symbols.quote: Stage $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ ($j$ now indexes stages) varies $a_j$.

symbols.name: earlier tensor space
symbols.meaning: The tensor power of F with j-1 factors, of dimension h^{j-1}.
symbols.quote: In one invocation, $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)}$ contains the line $P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ of earlier factors, with complement $B=P^\perp$; $Q=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ is the line of later factors.

symbols.name: earlier line
symbols.meaning: The line in A spanned by the tensor product of the indicators of the earlier triples a_1,...,a_{j-1}.
symbols.quote: In one invocation, $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)}$ contains the line $P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ of earlier factors, with complement $B=P^\perp$; $Q=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ is the line of later factors.

symbols.name: complement of P
symbols.meaning: The orthogonal complement of P in A.
symbols.quote: In one invocation, $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)}$ contains the line $P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ of earlier factors, with complement $B=P^\perp$; $Q=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ is the line of later factors.

symbols.name: larger subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of F containing G.
symbols.quote: of dimension $(h^{j-1}-1)\dim G+\dim E$; it lies in $[G'\mid E']$ whenever $G\subseteq G',\ E\subseteq E'$, as its parts lie in the orthogonal pieces $B\otimes F\otimes Q$ and $P\otimes F\otimes Q$.

symbols.name: next earlier space
symbols.meaning: The space A of the next stage, A tensor F.
symbols.quote: The next stage has $A'=A\otimes F$ and $P'=P\otimes\langle t_{a_j}\rangle$.

symbols.name: next earlier line
symbols.meaning: The line P of the next stage, P tensor the line of t_{a_j}.
symbols.quote: The next stage has $A'=A\otimes F$ and $P'=P\otimes\langle t_{a_j}\rangle$.

symbols.name: next complement
symbols.meaning: The orthogonal complement of P' in A', the B of the next stage.
symbols.quote: Splitting $A=B\perp P$ and $F=\langle t_{a_j}\rangle\perp t_{a_j}^\perp$ cuts $A'$ into four orthogonal pieces, and $B'=P'^\perp=(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t_{a_j}^\perp)$ is the other three.

symbols.name: next later line
symbols.meaning: The line Q of the next stage, spanned by the tensor product of the indicators of the triples after a_{j+1}.
symbols.quote: With $Q=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes Q'$ the outgoing labels are $A'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes Q'$ and $B'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes Q'$, the next incoming labels.

symbols.name: projection
symbols.meaning: The projection onto U along its orthogonal complement, the matrix at a vertex labelled U.
symbols.quote: In the bit network a vertex labelled $U$ gets the projection $\Pi_U$ onto $U$ along $U^\perp$, except sources: $-\Pi_{U_a}$ at $X_a$, else $0=\Pi_0$.

symbols.name: larger subspace
symbols.meaning: A nondegenerate subspace containing U.
symbols.quote: For nondegenerate $U\subseteq U'$, a vector of $U'$ minus its projection onto $U$ lies in $U'\cap U^\perp$, so $\mathcal F=U\perp(U'\cap U^\perp)\perp U'^\perp$.

Dimension counting rests on three facts about [tensor products of subspaces](tensor-product-of-spaces.md): for subspaces $E,E',G$ of tensor powers of $F$, $\dim(E\otimes G)=\dim E\cdot\dim G$; the form multiplies factorwise, so products of nondegenerate subspaces are nondegenerate; and $(E\perp E')\otimes G=(E\otimes G)\perp(E'\otimes G)$.

derivations.quote: Triples $S,S'\in\mathcal T$ have indicator vectors $t_S,t_{S'}$ with dot product $|S\cap S'|$ and entry sums $3$, so $\langle t_S,t_{S'}\rangle=|S\cap S'|-1$, or $|S\cap S'|\bmod2$ over $\mathbb F_2$. Hence each *triple line* $\langle t_S\rangle$ (its span) is nondegenerate, as $\langle t_S,t_S\rangle\in\{2,1\}$, and *neighbours* are orthogonal: triples sharing one element (bit), or distinct triples sharing zero or two (complex).
Source dimensions sum to $N$, sink dimensions to $Nm+N(m-1)+(W-2N)m=Wm-N$.
A wire enters and leaves each gate with that gate's label, so its signed changes telescope to sink minus source dimension, summing to $Wm-2N$ over all wires.

The next stage has $A'=A\otimes F$ and $P'=P\otimes\langle t_{a_j}\rangle$. Splitting $A=B\perp P$ and $F=\langle t_{a_j}\rangle\perp t_{a_j}^\perp$ cuts $A'$ into four orthogonal pieces, and $B'=P'^\perp=(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t_{a_j}^\perp)$ is the other three. With $Q=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes Q'$ the outgoing labels are $A'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes Q'$ and $B'\otimes\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\rangle\otimes Q'$, the next incoming labels. Stage 1 starts at $U_a$ and $0$; stage 3 ends at $\mathcal F$ and, as $P'=U_a$ there, $U_a^\perp$.

Comparing entries, every arrow is an inclusion except centre $3\to4$, which drops $P\otimes F\otimes Q$ of dimension $h$; side $2\to5$ needs $\langle t_X\rangle\subseteq t_Y^\perp$, true as neighbours are orthogonal.

Rows sharing a time meet at that gate. All labels are nondegenerate, like their pieces. Each of the $I=3v^2$ invocations has $c_{\rm b}=100$ or $c_{\rm c}=101$ centre wires, each losing $h$, so $L_{\rm b}=Ic_{\rm b}h$ and $L_{\rm c}=Ic_{\rm c}h$.

For nondegenerate $U\subseteq U'$, a vector of $U'$ minus its projection onto $U$ lies in $U'\cap U^\perp$, so $\mathcal F=U\perp(U'\cap U^\perp)\perp U'^\perp$. Both projections fix $U$ and vanish on $U'^\perp$, but only $\Pi_{U'}$ fixes $U'\cap U^\perp$, so $\Pi_{U'}-\Pi_U$ projects onto $U'\cap U^\perp$ and has rank $\dim U'-\dim U$, as does its negative on a reversed edge. So each edge's rank is its absolute dimension change, except the first edge of each $X_a$: at stage 1, $B=0$, so it joins $U_a$ to $[F\mid\langle t_{a_1}\rangle]=U_a$ with zero change, yet its matrix $\Pi_{U_a}-(-\Pi_{U_a})=2\Pi_{U_a}$ has image the line $U_a$ and rank one.
